balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

automotiveMargin.title: Automotive return on sales and EBITDA margin
automotiveMargin.content:
Automotive Return on Sales (RoS) is the operating margin of the Automotive segment alone -- the number Porsche management guides to each year. Automotive EBITDA margin is the equivalent before depreciation and amortisation.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: both are reported separately from the consolidated group because the Financial Services segment (captive leasing/financing) carries its own low-margin, high-turnover economics that would dilute the automotive story if blended in. RoS collapsed from 18.6% (FY2023) to 0.3% (FY2025) on China weakness, BEV/model-mix costs and realignment charges -- the central thesis-relevant number on this dashboard.

What to watch:

  • Whether RoS stabilises or keeps falling toward FY2026
  • The gap between RoS and EBITDA margin (depreciation/amortisation intensity from EV tooling)
  • Guidance updates versus the realised quarterly print

deliveries.title: Vehicle deliveries
deliveries.content:
Deliveries is the number of vehicles handed to customers in the period -- Porsche's unit-volume driver, distinct from Revenue (which also reflects price, mix and currency).

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: FY2025 deliveries fell to 279,449 from FY2023's peak of 320,221, driven mainly by China and the BEV transition (Taycan); the margin-collapse story (see Automotive RoS) is volume plus mix, not volume alone.

What to watch:

  • Whether volume decline is broad-based or concentrated in one region/model
  • Divergence between delivery growth and revenue growth (price/mix offsetting or amplifying volume)

deliveriesByModel.title: Deliveries by model line
deliveriesByModel.content:
Annual deliveries split by model line: 911 (halo sports car, highest margin), 718 Boxster/Cayman, Macan and Cayenne (SUVs, volume and profit backbone), Panamera and Taycan (the BEV flagship).

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: Taycan deliveries roughly halved from FY2022's 34,801 to FY2025's 16,339 as the model aged ahead of a refresh, while 911 held up best (51,583 in FY2025, its strongest year shown) -- mix is shifting toward the highest-margin model even as total volume falls. Only reported annually, so this chart does not get the interim toggle.

What to watch:

  • 911 holding share of the mix (margin support)
  • Taycan/BEV recovery once the refreshed model ships
  • Macan's transition to BEV-only and its effect on volume

bevShare.title: BEV share of deliveries
bevShare.content:
BEV share is the percentage of deliveries that were fully battery-electric (Taycan and, increasingly, Macan).

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: the jump from 12.7% (FY2024) to 22.2% (FY2025) is a mix shift, not a Taycan rebound -- Taycan units actually fell in FY2025, so the share rise comes mostly from the Macan BEV ramp. Read this alongside the model-line chart, not as standalone evidence of BEV demand recovery.

What to watch:

  • Whether share gains come with rising or falling absolute BEV units
  • EU/China regulatory and incentive shifts that move BEV demand independent of Porsche's own execution

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
